name: albanian_03
context: A Facebook comment under a post by the National Institute of Public Health of Kosovo during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The comment is in Albanian, mostly the informal Kosovo (Gheg) dialect, often written without the letters ë and ç.

versions.analysis_for_next: The main failure is over-predicting negative: 125 neutral texts went to negative, against only 16 negative texts going to neutral. These annotators treat a wide range of mildly critical, joking or opinionated comments as neutral. That includes number-betting banter ('Prap Prishtina spe lshon kreun e tabeles'), ironic cheering for more cases ('Hajde ma gjall'), jokes to tagged friends, demands for measures, complaints about the post's format, political jabs ('Albin Kurti i ka fajet'), long civic lectures, and even mild doubts about the numbers. Negative should be reserved for clearly hostile or alarmed tone: insults, swearing, 'turp të kini' aimed at the institute, explicit claims of lying, despair about the rising toll, or sarcastic mockery of the institute. Positive also needs fixing. Relief at low numbers counts as positive ('So keq sa per fillim', 'sosht keq', 'Kur don zoti 0-0'), as do 'Amin', 'T'hajrit kofshin' and 'Lutem te jen te fundit'. A greeting to a tagged friend ('aje mirë', 'mbajuni', 'Mir se vini') is neutral, not positive. The new version makes neutral the default, narrows negative, and adds the word 'keq' (bad) used in phrases meaning 'not bad' to the positive cues.

Version 1 overcorrected. Negative recall fell from 158 to 64, with 106 negative texts now labelled neutral, so macro-F1 dropped from 72.7 to 68.9. These annotators do count as negative any frustration, distrust, mockery or alarm aimed at the institute, the government or citizens. Examples: suspicion of copy-paste or invented numbers ('Dje 226 sod 224 mos jeni tja bo copy paste'), sarcasm at the institute ('Bajat jeni bo', 'si bastore', 'si KEK-u'), blaming politicians ('Fajet i ka Albin Kurti...'), alarm ('E hupi kontrollen', 'Prishtina si bomb atomice'), scolding people ('budall', 'Shqiptarit mos i thuj...') and angry demands ('Pse lejojne me na ardh nKosove pse???'). What stays neutral is playful banter among friends about which town leads the table, number guesses and bets without mockery of the institute, bare tags, plain questions, calm suggestions, and personal anecdotes. On the positive side, warm wishes to tagged people are positive ('perhajr', 'me shnet', 'Agron Cocaj perher'), as are relief and cheering for good news. Version 2 draws the negative boundary by target and tone: negative when criticism, sarcasm or alarm is directed at the institute, authorities, citizens or the worsening situation; neutral when it is light banter or information-seeking. This should sit between versions 0 and 1.

Version 2 swung too far towards negative: 198 neutral texts went to negative, so macro-F1 fell to 66.3. Version 0, at 72.7, remains the best. The boundary has to sit between versions 1 and 2. Across all three rounds, the texts annotators call negative are those that openly mock or distrust the institute or claim the numbers are fabricated: 'copy paste', 'rrena', 'bajat jeni bo', 'si bastore', 'si KEK-u', 'numra sa ju vyn'. Also negative are expressions of alarm or loss of control ('E hupi kontrollen', 'si bomb atomice', 'Kah po shkojmë'), insults and swearing. The texts annotators keep as neutral include pointed questions and pointed-out arithmetic mismatches without an accusation ('184+14=198 dhe jo 224', 'tash a 10 a 13???'). They also include demands and suggestions for measures, even in capitals or with exclamation marks ('Mbyllni kufijte sot!', 'HAPNI ÇERDHET!'), opinions about causes, short political remarks ('Albin Kurti i ka fajet..'), town-league banter, jokes to tagged friends and long civic lectures. So version 3 asks whether the comment's main point is an attack, accusation, mockery or alarm (negative) or a question, demand, opinion or joke (neutral). It adds contrast pairs for numbers questioned versus numbers called fake, and keeps the positive guidance from version 0, which worked well.

Version 3 is the best so far (macro-F1 77.2). Neutral-to-negative errors fell to 60 and negative-to-neutral errors are at 47. Many of the remaining errors look like inconsistent labels: 'Albin Kurti i ka fajet..' is neutral while 'Fajet i ka Albin Kurti Xhelal Sfeqla edhe Arben Vitia' is negative, and 'Hajde ma gjall' is positive in some texts and neutral in others. So I will keep the version 3 structure and make small, targeted edits. (1) Bare personal names that happen to be words ('Lum Rashiti', 'Shpresë Koliqi') were called positive; state that names alone are neutral, whatever they mean. Casual greetings to tagged friends ('aje mirë', 'mbajuni', 'Mir se vini') are also neutral; only blessing words make a tag positive. (2) Positive misses: 'T'hajrit kofshin' was called negative, so add it to the positive cues. Good news about recoveries ('ka lajm ma mir, 35 t'sherum', 'Super lajm') should be positive even with a request attached. Thanks followed by a question is positive. (3) Negative misses: some annotators mark as negative the comments that scold Albanians as a group ('Shqiptarit mos i thuj...', 'Gjithqfare budall ka Kosova') or say the institute is tired or careless ('Jeni lodh tybe', 'Kurqysh sun pi ndreqni qeto tabela'). Add these as narrow negative cues without broadening negative to all criticism.

Version 4 scored 80.2. The largest remaining error is still neutral texts labelled negative (62). Most of them fall into three groups. The first is humorous or wry quips, often with 'haha' or a tagged friend, that tease the lab or the posting ('Defekt aparatin e keni', 'Ja bre jeni vonu me rezultat ... Hahaha', 'Se di kush eshte ka e ban nervoz qata ne laborator'). The second is long civic lectures urging citizens to respect the rules, even passionate ones. The third is gloomy jokes about everyone getting infected. Annotators mark these neutral. The negatives the model still misses (30) are scattered and partly inconsistent, so I won't broaden negative. One change: scolding Albanians is only negative when it uses insult words ('budall', 'egoista'); a mere lecture is neutral. I will also add that teasing and dark humour without an accusation of faking are neutral. 'So keq sa per fillim' fell to negative, so 'so keq' (not bad) goes back into the positive cues. Everything else stays the same to protect the gains.

Version 5 (79.9) is essentially level with version 4 (80.2); the remaining errors are mostly ambiguous or inconsistently labelled. Three narrow fixes are still worth making. (1) Several cryptic, off-topic or unclear short texts were called negative ('Medal MEXAJULUTE...', 'Shes kepurdha', 'Mfal a bon 2buk', 'Kusho qikjo hajvalis', 'Dreni Musliu kqyre', 'Po nxen dilli po nxen hena...'). State that unclear, off-topic or untranslatable texts are neutral, and that only an evident hostile meaning makes a text negative. (2) Hope and encouragement were missed as positive ('shpresoj qe ta kalojmë këtë gjendje', 'vazhdojm me hapa te sigurt', 'Vushtrri qendro e fort'); add cues such as 'shpresoj' (I hope) and 'qendro e fort' (stay strong). (3) Joking guesses with 'haha' about towns keep drifting to negative, so I'll stress that the default is neutral when unsure. Everything else stays as in versions 4 and 5.

Version 6 (78.6) did worse than version 4 (80.2). The added 'when unsure, choose neutral' pushed 49 negatives to neutral: complaints at the authorities, sarcastic number jokes aimed at the institute, and complaints about being refused tests. The new 'shpresoj' cue also produced false positives on number guesses. So version 7 goes back to version 4's balance and keeps only the safe part of version 6: cryptic or off-topic texts are neutral. Two narrow additions for negative: bitter complaints that the authorities fail people (refusing tests, acting too late) and calls for the government to resign. 'Mir osht' and 'sosht keq' about the numbers stay positive. Hope counts as positive only when it is a sincere wish about the epidemic, not a number guess. I shortened the wording to stay under 400 words.

Version 7 (76.3) showed again how sensitive the model is to wording. Adding 'complaint' to the question and a negative category for bitter complaints about the authorities pushed 116 neutral texts to negative: demands, gripes about testing, political remarks and banter. The more neutral-leaning version 6 lost negatives instead. The best balance was version 4 (80.2), with version 5 close behind (79.9). So version 8 returns to version 4's wording almost unchanged. It keeps only two safe additions. (1) Cryptic or off-topic texts are neutral. Several, such as 'Medal...', 'Kusho qikjo hajvalis' and 'Dreni Musliu kqyre', keep being called negative. (2) 'So keq' (not bad) stays in the positive cues, since 'So keq sa per fillim' keeps flipping to negative. It drops the 'complaint' wording, the resignation cue and the 'when unsure, choose neutral' default. Remaining errors such as 'coppy paste' marked neutral are label noise, so I'm not chasing them.

Version 8 is the best so far (macro-F1 81.0). It returned to version 4's wording and added two safe changes: cryptic texts are neutral, and 'so keq' is a positive cue. The remaining errors are spread thinly, and many are inconsistent labels. For example, 'Qetu ne Gjilan... coppy paste' is gold neutral while similar copy-paste texts are gold negative, and 'Hajde ma gjall' is labelled both positive and neutral. Every bigger shift in the boundary (versions 1, 2, 6 and 7) hurt one class more than it helped another. For this final version I make only one micro-change. A small group of neutral texts are teasing remarks to tagged friends about their town or habits ('Ardita A. Ibrahimi a e keni pervluu çajiin', 'Leutrim Arjanit Q vitiaa so te lshu fronin', 'Dreni Musliu kqyre'). The model still sends these to negative, so I make 'teasing a tagged friend' explicit in the neutral description and cues. Everything else stays word for word.

Version 9 (79.9) did not improve on version 8 (81.0). Making 'teasing tagged friends' explicit did not fix those texts: 'Ardita A. Ibrahimi...' and 'Dreni Musliu kqyre' were still called negative, and a few other texts flipped. The ups and downs across versions 4, 5, 8 and 9 (80.2, 79.9, 81.0, 79.9) show a plateau of about 80. What remains is mostly label noise, such as 'coppy paste' gold neutral against 'copy paste' gold negative, 'Hajde ma gjall' labelled both positive and neutral, and blaming Albin Kurti gold neutral in one comment and negative in another. Every larger boundary shift (versions 1, 2, 6 and 7) cost more than it gained. For the final version I therefore restore version 8 word for word, since it gave the best balance between neutral and negative and the best positive recall.
